what_it_does: This paper ports hydrodynamic simulations—mathematical models that predict how fluids flow and behave—from traditional CPUs and GPUs to Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs). FPGAs are reprogrammable hardware chips that excel at energy efficiency and can be customized for specific workloads. The authors implemented 2D and 3D hydrodynamics solvers on Intel Agilex 7 FPGAs, using optimizations to exploit FPGA's large on-chip memory for data reuse and domain decomposition techniques that enable multiple processing pipelines to run in parallel across multiple FPGAs.
